# Records service API reference

<!-- Generated by tools/apidoc.py from docstrings. Do not edit by hand. -->

## `recordsvc.store`

In-memory record store.

### class `RecordItem`

One record of the admin tool.

Fields: `id`, `title`, `owner`, `status` (`active` or `archived`), and
`created_at` (ISO 8601, UTC).

### class `RecordStore`

Holds records in memory for the life of the process.

#### `RecordStore.list(status=None, owner=None, q=None)`

Return the records matching every given filter, ordered by `id`.

`status` and `owner` must match exactly; `q` is a case-insensitive
substring of the title. A filter left as `None` matches everything.

#### `RecordStore.get(record_id)`

Return the record with `record_id`, or `None` when there is none.

## `recordsvc.auth`

Users, roles, and server-side authorization for handlers.

### class `HttpError`

An error a handler turns into an HTTP status and a JSON `{"error": ...}` body.

### class `User`

A signed-in user with a `role` of `admin`, `editor`, or `viewer`.

### `authorize(user, allowed)`

Return `user` when its role is in `allowed`.

Raises `HttpError(401)` when `user` is `None` and `HttpError(403)` when the
role is not allowed.

### `require_admin(user)`

Return `user` if it is an administrator; see `authorize`.

Not used by any handler yet; kept for admin-only handlers.

## `recordsvc.filters`

Query parameter parsing shared by the handlers.

### `parse_filter(query)`

Build `RecordStore.list` keyword arguments from query parameters.

Values are trimmed; blank values and unknown parameters are ignored. A
`status` other than `active` or `archived` raises `HttpError(400)`.

## `recordsvc.export`

CSV serialization and export files.

### `csv_cell(value)`

Quote `value` when it contains a comma.

### `to_csv(records)`

Return a header row and one row per record, each ending with CRLF.

### `export_file_name(now)`

Return `export-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv` for the date of `now`.

### `write_export(directory, records, now)`

Write `to_csv(records)` to `directory/export-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv` and return the path.

## `recordsvc.api`

Request handlers and routing for the records service.

Handlers take the store, the signed-in user (or `None`), and the query
parameters, and return `(status, headers, body)`. The service has one route,
`GET /records`, handled by `list_records`.

### `list_records(store, user, query)`

Return the records matching `query` as JSON to any signed-in role.

The body is `{"count": n, "records": [...]}` with records ordered by `id`.
`query` accepts `status`, `owner`, and `q` (see `parse_filter`).

### `export_records(store, user, query, export_dir, now)`

Write the records matching `query` to a CSV file and return the CSV.

Uses the same filters as `list_records`. The file is written to
`export_dir/export-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv` and the response is 200 with the CSV
as the body.

### class `App`

The records service: a store seeded from `SEED_RECORDS` unless `records` is given.

Exports are written under `export_dir` (relative to the working directory)
and named from the UTC time returned by `now`.

#### `App.handle(method, path, user, query)`

Route a request and return `(status, headers, body)`.

An unknown path returns 404 and a known path with another method 405. An
`HttpError` raised by a handler becomes its status with a JSON `{"error": ...}`
body.
